What we can do at your place in Midlothian

1960s housing is the normal case in Midlothian. Masonry walls, wood trim, and most of that wood somewhere you need a ladder to reach. Which puts most of the cost in reach and in preparation. Painting a Midlothian house is not a wall-area job, it is a trim and access job.

The work we get called out to in Midlothian is exterior painting, interior painting and cabinet refinishing. Our own shop is at 7900 W. 83rd St. in Bridgeview, 9.0 straight-line miles from you, not a franchise desk in another county.

The parts of a Midlothian quote that actually move

The garage is half the exterior on a lot of 1964 plans and it is routinely left off the quote. What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is ranch, raised ranch and split-level, usually masonry to the sill line with frame gables above. Almost all the exterior paint in Midlothian sits above head height, which is why the work takes longer than the surface area suggests.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1964 median build year, and the split between 75.8 percent detached houses, 1.8 percent attached homes and 22.4 percent in buildings of two units or more.

That is inference and it is labeled as one. Wall material in Midlothian is not collected by any source behind this page, so there is no honest figure to put on it. Look at your own house and you will know more than this paragraph does.

Is there lead paint in my house?

If your house in Midlothian is the usual 1960s vintage, there is very likely old paint under whatever is on the walls now, and old paint can be leaded. Nobody has to leave a Midlothian house unpainted over it. It does mean the sanding, the sealing off and the cleanup are part of the job rather than an extra.

The practical content of it is dust. Where paint in a Midlothian room gets disturbed past about six square feet, twenty outside, or wherever a window comes out, the work has to be contained and cleaned to a standard. That is time at both ends of the job, and it is why an honest quote on 4,503 homes worth of 1964-median housing reads longer than a fast one.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Midlothian.

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 79.9 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Midlothian. Housing that old falls under the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, which covers any work disturbing paint in a home built before 1978. Illinois is not an authorized state for it, so EPA runs it here directly.

None of that is a reason to leave a Midlothian house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

Housing here runs to a median build year of 1964, and 79.9 percent of the 6,045 units in Midlothian predate 1980. 11 percent are prewar. Age is the first thing worth knowing about a house before it gets quoted, and it is the thing most quotes skip.

Behind the housing are 4,503 owner households and 1,331 renter households, 77.2 percent owner occupied. Of the units themselves, 22.4 percent are in buildings of two or more, 1.8 percent share a party wall as townhomes or rowhouses, and 75.8 percent stand on their own at a median 5.7 rooms. Median value across that stock is $200,300.

Where Midlothian departs most from the 76 place average: townhomes and rowhouses at 1.8 percent against a 7.5 percent average, prewar housing at 11 percent against a 15.8 percent average and detached houses at 75.8 percent against a 61.8 percent average.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

From the shop

Midlothian is mid 1960s stock, largely ranches, with a median value around $200,300 and almost all of it built well before 1978. On a 1960s ranch the exterior work concentrates into a narrow band: fascia, soffit, the garage door surround, the front entry and the window trim. Who actually shows up in Midlothian?

Mike Walsh owns the company, walks the job and stays on it while our crew works. Call 708-935-4289. It is worth saying because on a job this size the gap between whoever measured it and whoever turns up is where most of the disappointment comes from.

Can it be done a room at a time?

It can. Splitting a 5.7-room house into phases is normal and it is priced as phases rather than as a discount on the whole. The trade-off is setup time, because masking and protecting a room costs the same whether it is one room or the fourth.

What changes the price most on a house here?

The state of the trim and the ceilings. Wall area is predictable, and with 5.7 median rooms and a 1964 median build year in Midlothian the woodwork is where the hours actually go. Ask for it as its own line and the differences between two quotes stop being mysterious.
